The **Chief of Staff & Business Operations Manager for Vehicle Hardware Engineering (VHE)** is a leadership position reporting directly to the **Vice President of Vehicle Hardware Engineering**. In this high-impact role, you will lead and manage the dedicated **VHE Business Operations & Strategic Engineering Management Team**—the operational engine responsible for strategy, process governance, business performance, and cultural execution across global hardware engineering.  
  
As Chief of Staff, you serve as a strategic partner, trusted proxy, and operational integrator for the VP. You will lead your team to bridge Executive Leadership Team (ELT) objectives with ground-level engineering execution, transitioning VHE from a traditional product developer into an enterprise **Strategic Asset** delivering market-leading product quality, bulletproof reliability, and unmatched cost efficiency.  
  
The Chief of Staff leads, directs, and develops the VHE Business Operations team across five core functional pillars:  
  

* Executive Support & Chief of Staff Operations
* Executive Proxy & Stakeholder Alignment: Manage team members representing VHE across enterprise forums (Software, Program Management, Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality), ensuring hardware engineering standards and strategic priorities are advocated.
* Strategic Communications & Thought Leadership: Orchestrate high-stakes communications, drafting executive whitepapers, ELT presentation decks, board materials, and mass organizational updates on behalf of the VP.
* Leadership Alignment & Feedback Cadence: Establish structured governance loops between VP, Director, and Chief Engineer levels to accelerate decision-making, remove organizational silos, and maintain transparency.
* VP Priority Initiatives & Special Projects: Lead rapid-response cross-functional teams to resolve urgent operational, technical, or strategic challenges.
* Business Operations & Enterprise Governance
* Multi-Year Strategic Planning: Direct the multi-year planning process, converting ELT strategic objectives into actionable functional roadmaps (3-Year Strategy pillar of VHE Management System).
* Performance Management & Digital Dashboards: Oversee the design and implementation of automated, real-time KPI/OKR dashboards, providing unvarnished operational visibility across program execution.
* Enterprise SPoC Leadership: Serve as and manage the team acting as the primary Single Point of Contact (SPoC) for the Office of General Counsel (OGC), regulatory compliance bodies, and internal control test audits.
* Continuous Improvement & Efficiency Leadership
* Project Synergy & Efficiency Targets: Direct team initiatives to achieve efficiencies (2026–2030) and sustain 3% YoY engineering productivity gains across labor and non-labor spend.
* Operational Waste Elimination: Spearhead cross-functional problem-solving to eliminate engineering friction, increase 'time to engineer,' and optimize workflow execution.
* Organizational Strategy, Culture & Footprint
* HRO Cultural Integration: Institutionalize HRO practices and rapid iteration, fostering psychological safety to surface weak signals early and convert unknown risks into managed solutions.
* Education: Master’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration (MBA), or related technical management field required. Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, or Automotive Engineering strongly preferred.
* People Management & Team Leadership: 2+ years of direct experience managing high-performing teams of operational, process, or program management professionals within complex global manufacturing/automotive organizations.
* Progressive Engineering Experience: 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in automotive hardware engineering, D&R processes, GPDS vehicle gateways, FEDE BoM management, and B10 reliability standards.
* Process & Quality Mastery: Demonstrated expertise in 8D root-cause problem solving, Failure Mode Avoidance (FMA), DFMEA, Design for Manufacture & Assembly (DFM/DFA), and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE).
* Strategic & Business Acumen: Proven track record in multi-year strategic planning, engineering productivity modeling, ED&T should-cost analysis, prototype multiplier management, and footprint optimization.
* Executive Presence & Communication: Exceptional oral and written communication skills; ability to synthesize complex technical challenges, present to Executive Leadership Teams (ELT), and drive cross-functional consensus.
* High Reliability Leadership Mindset: Deep commitment to First-Principles thinking, intellectual humility, operational curiosity, and building safe, structural escalation mechanisms for technical risks.

Mechanical Design Engineering Manager

  

Location: Simsbury, CT   |   Reports to: Design Engineering Director

  

*Build Mechanical Design Capability. Improve Design Execution. Deliver Production-Ready Products.*

  

**Position Summary**

At Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company (EBAD), our products perform in environments where technical rigor, reliability, and safety are essential. The Mechanical Design Engineering Manager leads EBAD's Mechanical Design organization and strengthens mechanical design capability across the product-development lifecycle.

This leader owns the evolution of the mechanical design function supporting mission-critical aerospace and defense products, with responsibility spanning mechanical product design, enclosures, tooling, packaging, and rapid prototyping. The role builds the team, standards, capabilities, and operating practices needed to deliver production-ready designs with less rework while balancing manufacturability, assembly, testability, cost, safety, performance, and reliability.

  

**What You'll Do**

**Build and Lead the Mechanical Design Organization**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Mechanical Design team, with clear expectations, effective one-on-ones, candid feedback, development plans, accountability for results, and succession strength.

* Integrate the Simsbury and Moorpark Mechanical Design teams and activities—including product, enclosure, tooling, packaging, and rapid prototyping—under a common functional operating model.

* Build the team and capabilities needed for future growth by identifying critical skill gaps, supporting recruiting, and developing business cases for headcount and capital investment, including machining and 3D-printing capabilities.

**Strengthen Design Standards and Execution**

* Establish and improve mechanical design standards, methods, design reviews, release-readiness expectations, and operating cadence to make execution more consistent, scalable, and effective across sites and programs.

* Establish a consistent approach for prioritizing Mechanical Design resources across projects and aligning functional capacity with program needs.

* Strengthen Design for X (DfX) practices early in product development, balancing manufacturability, assembly, testability, cost, safety, performance, and reliability.

**Improve Product Quality and Technical Outcomes** 

* Deliver production-ready designs with less rework through disciplined tolerancing, design reviews, early validation, DFMEA, rapid prototyping, and collaboration with Operations and Supply Chain.

* Provide technical credibility and judgment in problem-solving discussions by assessing feasibility and risk, challenging assumptions, broadening the solution space, and removing obstacles without needing to be the subject-matter expert in every detail.

* Use the EBAD Operating System (EBOS) to reinforce operating cadence, visual management, structured problem solving, and kaizen within Mechanical Design.

**Influence Across the Business**

* Partner across Program Management, Business Development, Engineering, Operations, and customers to align mechanical design decisions with technical performance, manufacturability, cost, schedule, quality, configuration control, and customer outcomes.

* Influence product decisions from concept through production by enabling rapid prototyping and early validation and by resolving cross-functional tradeoffs before release.

* Translate complex mechanical design considerations into clear risks, recommendations, and business implications for senior leaders, customers, and cross-functional partners.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or another relevant technical discipline.

* At least 10 years of progressive mechanical engineering and product-development experience supporting complex aerospace, defense, space, or similarly demanding engineered products.

* Proven people leadership, including setting clear expectations, providing candid feedback, holding people accountable, and building team capability and succession strength.

* Strong mechanical design and product-development experience across the lifecycle from concept through production, including practical application of DfX principles.

* Strong technical competence and judgment sufficient to engage engineers in substantive problem-solving discussions, assess feasibility and risk, and guide decisions.

* Experience establishing or improving engineering standards, design reviews, release-readiness practices, or development processes that improve quality, speed, rigor, and predictability.

* Experience using structured, data-driven problem solving and continuous-improvement methods to improve engineering performance.

* Strong influence and communication skills, with the ability to partner effectively across engineering, operations, programs, business development, and customers.

**Experience That Would Set You Apart**

* Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or another relevant technical discipline preferred.

* Experience leading mechanical design organizations across multiple sites or product lines, including product design, enclosure design, tooling design, packaging design, and rapid prototyping.

# Senior Operations Manager - 2nd Shift

Dallas, TX

**Position Overview:**

The role oversees multiple reconditioning lines and is responsible to ensure necessary production metrics are consistently met.

**What you’ll be doing:**

* Oversee multiple reconditioning lines within the Inspection & Reconditioning Center (IC), planning production for a full working shift.
* Fully manage facilities to meet or exceed targets in production, cost, and quality when the General Manager is not onsite.
* Quickly identify bottlenecks that affect site throughput and efficiency. Conduct root cause analysis, develop action plans, and  execute with the site leadership team and associates.
* Conduct weekly site performance reviews with Senior Reconditioning leadership, reporting on performance versus targets, challenges, and countermeasures.
* Guide daily site manager huddles to establish the day’s tone and priorities.
* Aid in the execution of Continuous Improvement projects at home site and, if applicable, throughout the region/network, while implementing and training process changes.
* Foster growth and development in our Reconditioning Lead and Manager populations by supporting Development Plans and providing regular competency-based feedback.
* Embody Carvana values through effective leadership, teamwork, and communication on the shop floor.
* Uphold Carvana operating standards and processes.
* Ensure compliance with all health, safety and loss prevention guidelines.

**What the job requires:**

* Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.
* Experience leading a team of over 50 associates and a track record of developing employees.
* Proven ability to solve urgent operational challenges through root cause analysis.
* Excellent communication skills.
* 8+ years of management experience either in an automotive or lean manufacturing environment.
* Valid unrestricted driver’s license with a clean driving record in the last 3 years.
* Must be able to read, write, speak and understand English.
* Must be at least 18 years of age.
* Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance.
* Requires use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment.
* Ability to work variable schedule(s) as necessary.
* Must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently; majority of lifting from knee to shoulder heights; other lifting required from various levels.
* Must be able to walk up to three miles each day.

**Other requirements**  
To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

* Must be able to read, write, speak and understand English.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

# From Customer Service Representative to Plant President
## Inside this Leader’s 39-Year Journey at RRD Manchester
We sat down with RRD’s Corrie Duncan to discuss her nearly four-decade journey from entry-level employee to the first female president at the company’s Manchester facility, and leading in today’s manufacturing industry. ### Q: You recently became president of RRD’s Manchester facility. Tell us about your journey to this role.
**A:** My career started nearly 39 years ago at another RRD facility in Danbury, Connecticut, where I answered phones. From there, I moved into sales support, customer service, and eventually customer service leadership roles. In 2012, I transitioned to Manchester as customer service manager. Over the years, I’ve had the opportunity to learn every aspect of the business from client relationships and operations to production and fulfillment. Earlier this year, I was honored to step into the role of president for the Manchester facility. This also makes me the first female president of the Manchester plant. ### Q: What has kept you in the manufacturing and print industry for nearly four decades?
**A:** It’s an industry that’s constantly evolving. Many people still think of print as static production, but today’s environment is highly technical, data-driven and personalized. Every day brings a new challenge, whether it’s helping a healthcare client manage sensitive communications, supporting hospitality brands or developing customized fulfillment programs. I’ve always enjoyed the problem-solving aspect of the business and the relationships we build with clients over time. ### Q: How has RRD’s Manchester facility evolved in recent years?
**A:** The biggest shift has been the growth of personalized communications and fulfillment services. Today, RRD does far more than traditional printing. Our team supports highly customized variable-data printing, direct mail, warehousing, kitting and fulfillment programs for clients across industries including hospitality, healthcare and life sciences. We’ve also continued investing in digital technologies and workflows that allow us to produce highly targeted communications quickly and efficiently that increase engagement. ### Q: As a woman leading a manufacturing operation, what does this milestone mean to you?
**A:** I’m proud of the path that brought me here. Manufacturing has created opportunities for so many people willing to learn and grow within the industry. I’ve been fortunate to work alongside mentors and teams who supported my development over the years. I hope my journey shows that there are meaningful long-term careers in manufacturing and operations, and that leadership opportunities are achievable through experience, adaptability and hard work.
